Good morning. Let's get right into it for Wednesday, September 23rd. This edition is laser-focused on pre-market earnings and a major analyst day, so let's break down what matters for your trading day.

Starting with the biggest beat of the morning — Cracker Barrel. The stock posted a blowout fiscal Q4. Sales came in at $849 million versus the Street's $834 million estimate. Adjusted EPS was 99 cents — absolutely crushing the 16-cent consensus. EBITDA hit $62 million versus the $41.5 million expected. Now, tariff refunds were a tailwind, but even stripping those out, EBITDA was $53 million — still well above consensus. And looking into fiscal 2027, the EBITDA guidance mid-point of $190 million tops the Street's $177 million. This is a clean beat across the board. Bullish setup.

Next up, General Mills. The read here is "not as bad as feared." Fiscal Q1 EPS came in at 75 cents — down 13% on a foreign-exchange-neutral basis, but still above the 72-cent consensus. Organic revenue was roughly flat versus the Street's negative 1.8% estimate, and all four business segments beat on revenue. Gross margins fell 0.90% but came in at 33.3%, above the 33% estimate. Operating margins fell 1.30% to 14.4%, also ahead of the 13.8% forecast. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed. But here's the catch — Adam is flagging that sentiment toward food-focused staples is likely to stay gloomy given fierce cyclical and secular headwinds. Better-than-feared print, mixed overall. Watch how the stock trades on that tension.

Manchester United posted a modest fiscal Q4 beat — sales of 157.5 million British pounds topped the 145 million estimate, and EBITDA of 28.9 million came in above the 22 million consensus. But the forward guide is the problem. The fiscal 2027 EBITDA guidance mid-point of 215 million pounds falls well short of the 245 million the Street was expecting. Beat now, miss later — that's a mixed read and the guide miss is going to weigh.

Then there's McDonald's, which is holding its analyst meeting today. The headline target is an operating margin of low-to-mid 50% by 2030 — that is clearly above the current consensus forecast of 49.5%, which is a positive. The company is also increasing capital spending to drive growth, but that comes at a cost — free cash flow conversion is expected to shift down to the mid-to-high 80% range by 2030, from the prior goal of low-to-mid 90% set back in 2023. Adam's tone is measured — the margin target is a genuine beat versus consensus, but the strategic language around their new platform gets a bit of an eye-roll. Mixed, with the margin target as the key bull case.

Bottom line for today: CBRL is the cleanest long setup off this morning's prints. GIS is a relief trade but faces structural sector headwinds. MANU is weighed down by the guide miss. And MCD is all about whether the operating margin target can sustain buying interest through the analyst meeting. Stay focused, manage your risk, and good luck out there.
